about: Sections of an essay on romance by Joel (first person). In each, the sentences listed under "changed" were just rewritten; the rest is the essay as it stands. Read each section as it stands, with its heading.

texts.heading: And deeper is the point
changed: Or maybe they don’t, and you can’t make that a test of whether they love you.
sentences: Beyond all that practical stuff, sex is extremely important for building and renewing the connection.
I also think that if two people aren’t having sex, it becomes hard to explain how they’re different from regular friends.
But if the connection gets deep enough, sex appeal stops being the basis of the relationship.
You don’t stop loving the person because she got old, he lost his job, one of you got sick, or sex became impossible.
Sometimes they may even want you to find sexual satisfaction elsewhere if they can’t give it, because they love you and want you to be happy.
Or maybe they don’t, and you can’t make that a test of whether they love you.

texts.heading: My flaws
changed: Their meditations may have helped them a lot, but I still had no idea how either woman would act when a relationship got ugly, and somebody who starts with enough trauma can make huge progress and still have a lot left unresolved.

On my side, the blind spot is that I have trouble understanding where people are at mentally and emotionally, so a partner may agree with everything I say and then tell me later, “Didn’t you understand I was FAWNING?”
No, I really didn’t, so if you’re fawning, tell me when you can.
What’s happening in your head may feel obvious to you, but I can’t see it from outside.

texts.heading: If slow isn’t realistic for you
changed: Avoiding them has definitely saved me from having ten times the body count, but it doesn’t work reliably, because the invitation that leads there often starts out small, like “Hey, wanna go do something together?”
Those are light versions of the much stronger barriers that Islamic and conservative Christian cultures put around a man and woman being alone before marriage.
sentences: I pretty much always intend to wait long enough to have this conversation and figure out who I’m dealing with.
Then the heat of the moment hits and I want her to think of me as the guy who pleases her, not the guy who makes her think twice about wanting pleasure.
So my main strategy has been to avoid heat-of-the-moment situations until I’m ready.

Avoiding them has definitely saved me from having ten times the body count, but it doesn’t work reliably, because the invitation that leads there often starts out small, like “Hey, wanna go do something together?”
Maybe she wants me to come to an event, a meditation teaching, or a walk in nature.
Phone or video first can help, as can meeting up around other people and deciding beforehand that we aren’t going home together.
Those are light versions of the much stronger barriers that Islamic and conservative Christian cultures put around a man and woman being alone before marriage.
I don’t accept their helicoptering solution, but they noticed something real.
We don’t live in tribes anymore, where people around us might know both of us well enough to slow this down.

texts.heading: Some babies grow up faster
sentences: “I’m sad, what should I do?”
I usually had some idea, so of course I answered, but enough moments become a pattern.
Key at first asked me innocently, “Can you be my guru?”
I told her, “I’m not anyone’s guru, but we can learn from each other.”
A few months later, she was telling me she was much more spiritually advanced than me.
I asked, “Do you recall asking me to be your guru?”
She said, “Wow, I must have been really confused back then!”
I also have to admit, I can become condescending when somebody stops taking responsibility for their behavior.
I find that intolerable.
If someone tells me, “I feel like your patient,” we both have to look at what we’re doing.
I know what happens on my side.
Helping feels good, and so does being needed.
A lot of the time I really did have the answer or the perspective they needed, so of course they kept asking me.
I also had to look at whether they were trying to take care of themselves without me.

texts.heading: Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up
changed: If one person goes down, the other becomes the whole backup system, covering the housing and the money, looking after the children and handling whatever health or emotional crisis comes up, so who even has time for the relationship itself at that point?

Maybe an unusually strong couple can get away without much outside support, but I think that’s rare, because it’s often a friend who actually knows us both who sees the dysfunctional pattern before either of us does.
They’re helpful when you need privacy from your partner and somewhere else to say what you’re feeling.
Take what they say with a grain of salt, since they’re only hearing your side, usually while you’re upset, and they may just be trying to protect you.
sentences: Even if I found my twin flame, she’d still be one person.
The polarity could be perfect and we’d still need other people around us.
Here’s how this looks for me: whenever something serious comes up in my relationships, we each run to our own friends for support.
Then I resent the one-sided story she’s telling, she resents the one-sided story I’m telling.
Some of the friends may even be exes who want us to break up, and eventually neither of us wants to talk to the other’s friends anymore.
That’s a pretty terrible time to be trying to run the rest of life with two people.

If one person goes down, the other becomes the whole backup system, covering the housing and the money, looking after the children and handling whatever health or emotional crisis comes up, so who even has time for the relationship itself at that point?

Maybe an unusually strong couple can get away without much outside support, but I think that’s rare, because it’s often a friend who actually knows us both who sees the dysfunctional pattern before either of us does.
On the other hand, If both people are falling apart, there is only so much anyone else can do.
Separate confidants can be helpful and harmful.
They’re helpful when you need privacy from your partner and somewhere else to say what you’re feeling.
But if your confidant doesn’t have a good connection with your partner, the conversation can turn into an echo chamber very easily.
Having the same confidant creates the opposite problem: now you may not have a release valve when you want privacy from your partner, so neither way is perfect.
If you do have separate confidants, you need enough emotional maturity to remember they will automatically be biased toward you.
Take what they say with a grain of salt, since they’re only hearing your side, usually while you’re upset, and they may just be trying to protect you.

texts.heading: Doing it consciously 🧭 + Imagination as a discernment tool
changed: Rewind: what if we disagree on having kids?
Fast forward five years: what has each of us gained or given up, and do we have any resentment about it?
And if psychedelics are involved, every scene can look even more beautiful, so they make this same problem of idealization much stronger.
sentences: Rewind: what if we disagree on having kids?
Fast forward five years: what has each of us gained or given up, and do we have any resentment about it?
This isn’t to make predictions and we’re not consulting the magic 8 ball nor doing Istikhara rituals here.
I mean you can do that too if you want.
Distinguish between fears and what really seems likely just as you do between wishes and reality.
If every scene is beautiful, consider that you may be, and almost certainly are, still rehearsing the relationship you want.
There’s nothing wrong with expecting the best, but it takes work to get there in a wise way.
And if psychedelics are involved, every scene can look even more beautiful, so they make this same problem of idealization much stronger.

texts.heading: If you’re already in it
changed: If the two of you are stuck there, that’s when you need agape the most, because the best thing for both of you may not be holding onto the relationship pattern you originally committed to or dreamt of.
If that’s where things are at, ouch, the trust is out the window.
sentences: Some things were less mysterious: they were acting as if the trust problem wasn’t there because they still wanted the relationship.
Attractions to other people sometimes went unsaid too, and sometimes got imagined from nowhere.
Some people keep a relationship like this going for a long time, just sweeping everything under the rug.
On the other hand, sometimes I was more honest than my partner could handle, which was its own kind of damage.
Ask whether both of you actually want to prioritize radical honesty, first.
But the other person also can’t keep saying “not now” forever and think that’s going to save the relationship.

If the two of you are stuck there, that’s when you need agape the most, because the best thing for both of you may not be holding onto the relationship pattern you originally committed to or dreamt of.
When did you two last dance?
And not the “we dance around our problems” joke (LOL)..
If that’s where things are at, ouch, the trust is out the window.
I know that one from experience with my first 2 wives and K, too.
That generally marks the point of no return, so try not to wait for that.
Because once you’re there, as my dad explained a thousand times whenever we had a visitor, unconscious resentment begins to snowball, and we feel colder together than alone.
Pretty soon, old Romeo & Juliette might get wandering eye syndrome.
